title: Report: Cycling to school
text:
Report on cycling to school

Introduction
This report has been prepared for the town council following last year's decision to build two new cycle lanes near secondary schools. Its purpose is to assess whether the lanes have encouraged more students to cycle and to identify remaining obstacles. The information comes from a questionnaire answered by 600 students at three schools and from bicycle counts carried out by volunteers in October.

How students travel
Before the new lanes were built, only 9% of students cycled to school. According to this year's questionnaire, the figure has risen to 21%. The bicycle counts confirm this trend: on an average weekday, the number of bikes parked at the three schools more than doubled. Walking remains the most popular way of getting to school (38%), while the proportion of students driven by their parents has fallen from 35% to 24%.

Reasons for not cycling
Students who do not cycle gave three main reasons. The most frequently mentioned was safety: many said that the cycle lanes end suddenly at busy crossroads, which makes the last part of the journey dangerous. The second reason was the lack of secure parking – several students had had their bikes stolen. Finally, a significant number of respondents said they had nowhere to change or leave wet clothes on rainy days.

Recommendations
It is recommended that the council extend the cycle lanes so that they connect directly to school entrances. Covered and locked bicycle parking should be provided at all three schools. In addition, schools could be encouraged to offer lockers for students who cycle.

Conclusion
The new lanes have clearly had a positive impact. Nevertheless, unless the safety and parking problems are addressed, it is unlikely that the number of cyclists will continue to grow.
